newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends at lows on liquidation.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends at lows on liquidation.

text.p: CSCE world sugar prices closed at the day's lows, pressured by technically-driven speculative selling, floor sources said.

Friday's weak close and the committment of traders report, which showed the funds and the speculators to have a much higher net long position than players had anticipated, fueled losses early, one trader said.
"It gave the impression that there is more liquidation to do, and with Friday's weaker close, that is exactly what happened," he said.
While the trade remained a steady buyer as prices continued to slide, the selling overpowered the attempt to hold the March contract above resistance at 10.35.
March closed down 0.17 cents to 10.35, after trading 10.47 to 10.34 cents. The back months ended 0.13 to 0.02 lower.
Volume was estimated at 25,074 lots, with the bulk of activity attributed to speculative liquidation.

Dealers pegged resistance basis the March contract at 10.50. They said March will need to remain above this level in order to dissuade players from putting on new short positions amid an ongoing dearth of physical offtake.
"If the market continues to show weakness we will see the speculative liquidation turn to new selling," a trader said. "With no physical offtake, no one is inspired to do any buying."
He noted a gap on the charts between Friday's low of 10.50 cents, and today's high of 10.47 cents, basis March.
